intro.say: At night we can see the Moon and lots of twinkly stars. Let us look up!

rounds.say: The Moon is a big ball of rock. It goes round and round our Earth.
rounds.caption: the Moon

rounds.say: Stars look like tiny twinkly dots, but they are really giant balls of hot, glowing gas, very, very far away.
rounds.caption: stars

rounds.ask: What goes round and round the Earth?

options.label: a cloud
options.why: Clouds float in our sky; they do not go round Earth.

options.label: a bird
options.why: Birds fly near the ground, not round the Earth.

rounds.explain: The Moon travels all the way round the Earth.

rounds.ask: What is the Moon made of?

options.label: cheese
options.why: That is a fun story, but the Moon is not cheese!

options.label: fire
options.why: The Sun and stars glow hot; the Moon is cold rock.

rounds.explain: The Moon is a big ball of rock and dust.

rounds.ask: Why do stars look so small?

options.label: they are tiny
options.why: Stars are really huge!

options.label: they are toys
options.why: Stars are real, giant and glowing, not toys.

rounds.explain: Stars are giant, but they are so far away that they look like dots.

rounds.ask: Which can you see in the night sky?

options.label: a rainbow
options.why: Rainbows need sunshine and rain in the day.

rounds.explain: On a clear night the sky is full of stars.

intro.say: The Moon seems to change shape. Let us find out why!

rounds.say: The Moon has no light of its own. The Sun shines on it, and we see the sunny part.
rounds.caption: sunlight on the Moon

rounds.say: As the Moon goes round Earth, we see more or less of its sunny side. So it looks like a new shape each night. These are its phases.
rounds.caption: phases

rounds.say: When we see all of the sunny side, it is a full Moon. When we see none of it, it is a new Moon.
rounds.caption: full Moon · new Moon

rounds.ask: Where does moonlight really come from?

options.label: a lamp on the Moon
options.why: There are no lamps on the Moon.

options.label: the Moon makes it
options.why: The Moon has no light of its own.

rounds.explain: Moonlight is sunlight bouncing off the Moon.

rounds.ask: Which one is a full Moon?

options.label: crescent
options.why: That is only a thin slice.

options.label: half
options.why: That is a half Moon.

rounds.explain: A full Moon is a whole bright circle.

rounds.ask: Does the Moon really change shape?

options.label: yes, it shrinks
options.why: The Moon stays the same size and shape.

options.label: no, we see different parts lit

rounds.explain: The Moon is always round; we just see different amounts of its sunny side.

rounds.ask: The Moon is growing! Put the shapes in order, starting with the new Moon.
rounds.explain: From new Moon, the bright part gets bigger each night until it is full.

rounds.ask: About how long does the Moon take to go all the way round Earth?

options.label: one day
options.why: One day is how long Earth takes to spin.

options.label: one year
options.why: A year is Earth going round the Sun.

rounds.explain: The Moon takes about a month to go round Earth, so its shapes repeat every month.

intro.say: The Sun is a star too! Let us learn about stars and the pictures they make.

rounds.say: The Sun is a star, the closest one to Earth. Other stars are suns too, but they are so far away they look tiny.
rounds.caption: the Sun is our closest star

rounds.say: Long ago, people joined stars with pretend lines to make pictures, like a bear or a hunter. These star pictures are called constellations.
rounds.caption: constellations

rounds.say: Stars are in the sky in the daytime too. The Sun is so bright that we cannot see them.
rounds.caption: stars by day

rounds.ask: Which star is closest to Earth?

options.label: the North Star
options.why: It is very far away.

options.label: the Moon
options.why: The Moon is not a star; it is rock.

rounds.explain: The Sun is a star, and it is the nearest star to us.

rounds.ask: Why do we not see stars in the daytime?

options.label: they go to sleep
options.why: Stars shine all the time.

options.label: they fall down
options.why: Stars do not fall out of the sky.

rounds.explain: The bright Sun hides the fainter stars, but they are still there.

options.label: a kind of moon
options.why: A constellation is made of stars, not moons.

options.label: a space rocket
options.why: Rockets are machines people build.

rounds.explain: A constellation is a group of stars that people imagine as a picture.

rounds.ask: The Sun looks much bigger than other stars. Why?

options.label: it is the only big star
options.why: Many stars are as big as the Sun or bigger.

options.label: it is much closer to us
it is a planet
options.why: The Sun is a star, not a planet.

rounds.explain: Things look bigger when they are close; the Sun is the closest star.

rounds.ask: The Moon looks brighter than the stars. Is it a star?

options.label: yes, the brightest star
options.why: It looks bright, but it makes no light.

rounds.explain: The Moon is close and reflects sunlight, but it makes no light, so it is not a star.

rounds.ask: Does it make its own light?
rounds.explain: The Sun, stars and fire glow with their own light; the Moon and planets only reflect sunlight.
